He dies, and his son reigns in his stead; a later Laman, named after his father, rules a numerous people and appoints teachers.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mosiah
s: The Nephites are a people associated with the lands of Lehi-Nephi, Shilom, Zarahemla, and Zeniff’s people. After conflict involving Zeniff’s brethren and army, Zeniff’s people return to Zarahemla, settle in the land of Nephi, and possess land in peace for twenty-two years. They cultivate grain, fruit, and many seeds, keep flocks, make fine linen and cloth, and maintain weapons. Trusting in the Lord, they protect their women and children, fight the Lamanites, defeat them, and return to their land. Later, the people of Limhi are surrounded, oppressed, guarded, and afflicted by the Lamanites, required to pay half of all they possess as tribute; Limhi prefers slavery to the Nephites and expects deliverance. The Nephites ultimately inhabit Zarahemla as the people among whom the reign of judges begins.

l: bondage, The Book of Mosiah
s: Bondage is the subjection of Limhi’s people to the Lamanites, brought on by their iniquities and abominations. It burdens, afflicts, and drives them, motivating a search for Zarahemla and deliverance. Limhi teaches that God will deliver them if they turn to him and serve diligently. After humbling themselves, their burdens are eased; Gideon’s plan finally enables their departure.

l: taxation, The Book of Mosiah
s: Taxation is a grievous burden imposed on the people. Under Limhi, they pay the Lamanites half their crops, herds, and possessions or lose their lives. Under Noah, one fifth of possessions supports Noah, his wives and concubines, and priests, making the people labor exceedingly for iniquity.

l: sin, The Book of Mosiah
s: Sin is rebellion and transgression against God. It brings divine judgment, bondage, afflictions, and a fallen state, as seen among Limhi’s people and those led by flattering words. People are warned to repent; confession and sincere repentance bring forgiveness, while refusal excludes people from the church.

l: affliction, The Book of Mosiah
s: is_a great suffering [of the people of Limhi] The people of Limhi suffered great affliction, including bondage, tribute, and the deaths of many brethren. Limhi said their affliction resulted from transgression and gave them reason to mourn.

l: prophet of the Lord, The Book of Mosiah
s: A chosen prophet warned people of wickedness, foretold Christ’s coming, and was slain after delivering his message.

l: contentions, The Book of Mosiah
s: Mosiah warns that replacing or dethroning kings can cause contention and much bloodshed among the people.

l: promise of the Lord, The Book of Mosiah
s: is_fulfilled people of Limhi [through their affliction and bondage] The promise of the Lord was fulfilled when the people were smitten and afflicted because of their wickedness. The Lord also promised that he would deliver them if they turned to him and served him with diligence.

l: deliverance from bondage, The Book of Mosiah
s: Deliverance from bondage is promised by the Lord if Limhi’s people turn to him and serve him. Limhi teaches that they must trust God, then the people cry mightily for relief. Their burdens are eased as Lamanite hearts soften, but they remain captive. Unable to win by the sword, they escape through a secret pass using Gideon’s plan.

l: brethren in the land of Zarahemla, The Book of Mosiah
s: are_in land of Zarahemla The brethren in the land of Zarahemla are the people whose history Ammon recounts to Limhi’s people, from the time Zeniff left until Ammon came up out of Limhi’s land.

l: forty-three people sent into the wilderness, The Book of Mosiah
s: Forty-three people were sent to find Zarahemla and seek deliverance for Limhi’s brethren. Lost in the wilderness, they traveled many days, found a land among many waters with evidence of destroyed people, and returned with twenty-four plates as testimony.

l: people who had been destroyed, The Book of Mosiah
s: A people who once populated a discovered land as numerously as Israel are traced from Adam through the great tower; their bones, ruins, and records may reveal their identity and destruction.

l: discovered land of the destroyed people, The Book of Mosiah
s: A land once peopled by a numerous people later destroyed, covered with dry bones of men and beasts, ruins, and artifacts. Men sent by Limhi discover it, suppose it Zarahemla, and return with a record of its people.

l: plates containing the record of Limhi's people, The Book of Mosiah
s: The plates containing the record of Limhi’s people were brought before Ammon so he could read them. Their record was made from the time Limhi’s people left the land of Zarahemla.

l: plates of gold, The Book of Mosiah
s: Plates of pure gold, filled with engravings recording a destroyed people, are brought from a discovered land by Limhi’s people and delivered to king Mosiah. Though initially uninterpretable, Mosiah translates them with interpreters; the account gives his people much knowledge and causes them to mourn exceedingly.
